prompt: Company profile: Regional homebuilder based in Marietta, Georgia; 60 employees. Situation: The company is about to clear and grade a 3.5-acre phase of a new subdivision (part of a larger 25-acre common plan of development). Georgia EPD administers the NPDES program and the state erosion and sedimentation law. Ask: Identify the compliance obligations this situation creates or affects for the compliance-obligations register. For each obligation: state the requirement, its source, its applicability to this company, the ISO clause it maps to (ISO 14001 6.1.3 / ISO 45001 6.1.3), and how and when compliance should be evaluated (9.1.2).
response:
**Compliance Obligations Register – Marietta Homebuilder (3.5-Acre Land Disturbance)**

---

### **Obligation 1: NPDES Construction General Permit Coverage**
- **Requirement**: Obtain coverage under Georgia NPDES General Permit GA-G870000 (Construction General Permit) by submitting a Notice of Intent (NOI) *before* commencing land disturbance. Develop and implement a site-specific Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plan (SWPPP) that identifies Best Management Practices (BMPs) to control erosion and prevent sediment discharge. Maintain permit coverage until final stabilization is achieved and a Notice of Termination (NOT) is approved.
- **Source**: Clean Water Act §402; 40 CFR 122; Georgia Rules 391-3-6-.15; GA-G870000 Parts III.A & III.D
- **Applicability**: Directly applies as land disturbance of 3.5 acres exceeds the 1-acre threshold for mandatory NPDES permit coverage. The 25-acre common plan of development triggers additional sediment basin requirements (Rule 391-3-7-.07(6)(a)).
- **ISO Clause**: ISO 14001:2015 6.1.3 (compliance obligations); ISO 45001:2018 6.1.3 (legal requirements – construction safety)
- **Evaluation (9.1.2)**: 
  - *How*: Verify NOI approval status, SWPPP completeness, BMP installation, and NOT submission through quarterly internal audits and annual third-party environmental compliance audit. Review inspection logs weekly.
  - *When*: Before ground disturbance, monthly during active construction, and upon project phase completion.

---

### **Obligation 2: Georgia Erosion & Sedimentation Act (GESA) Permit**
- **Requirement**: Obtain a Land Disturbing Activity (LDA) permit from the local issuing authority (Cobb County Water System or City of Marietta) *prior* to clearing/grading. Develop and implement an Erosion, Sedimentation, and Pollution Control Plan (ES&PCP) certified by a qualified professional. Comply with all permit conditions, including perimeter controls, sediment barriers, and stabilization requirements.
- **Source**: O.C.G.A. §12-7-1 *et seq.*; Georgia Rule 391-3-7-.07; Cobb County Development Standards (Sec. 34-81)
- **Applicability**: Mandatory for any land disturbance > 1 acre in Georgia. As a 60-employee homebuilder, the company is a "land developer" under GESA and must comply with local implementation of state law.
- **ISO Clause**: ISO 14001:2015 6.1.3; ISO 45001:2018 6.1.3 (operational controls for workplace hazards)
- **Evaluation (9.1.2)**:
  - *How*: Confirm permit issuance and conditions during pre-construction review. Conduct monthly site inspections by certified personnel to verify ES&PCP implementation. Review violation notices and corrective actions.
  - *When*: Prior to start, monthly during active disturbance, and within 48 hours of any rainfall event > 0.5 inches.

---

### **Obligation 3: Certified Personnel & Training**
- **Requirement**: Employ or contract a Level 1B Certified Professional (Plan Preparer) to design the ES&PCP and a Level 1B Certified Person (Site Manager) to supervise land-disturbing activities. Ensure all site supervisors complete OSHA 30-Hour Construction Training and Georgia Erosion Control Certification.
- **Source**: O.C.G.A. §12-7-8; Georgia Rule 391-3-7-.07(7); 29 CFR 1926.21 (OSHA training)
- **Applicability**: Required for all LDA permits > 1 acre. As the "responsible party," the company must verify certifications for any employees or contractors performing supervisory roles.
- **ISO Clause**: ISO 14001:2015 6.1.3 (competence); ISO 45001:2018 6.1.3 & 7.2 (competence & training)
- **Evaluation (9.1.2)**:
  - *How*: Audit personnel certification records annually for currency (renewal every 3 years). Verify OSHA training cards during new hire onboarding and quarterly field audits. Include in contractor prequalification checklists.
  - *When*: Before personnel begin work, annually, and within 24 hours of any personnel changes.

---

### **Obligation 4: Stormwater Inspection & Monitoring**
- **Requirement**: Conduct documented inspections of erosion/sediment controls at least once every 7 days *and* within 24 hours of rainfall events > 0.5 inches. Maintain signed inspection logs, photograph deficiencies, and implement corrective actions within 72 hours. Submit annual compliance summary to Georgia EPD.
- **Source**: GA-G870000 Part IV.B; Georgia Rule 391-3-7-.07(8); 40 CFR 122.41
- **Applicability**: Mandatory for all active NPDES and GESA permittees. The 3.5-acre phase requires continuous monitoring until final stabilization.
- **ISO Clause**: ISO 14001:2015 6.1.3 & 9.1.1 (monitoring); ISO 45001:2018 6.1.3 & 9.1.1 (workplace inspections)
- **Evaluation (9.1.2)**:
  - *How*: Review inspection logs weekly for completeness, signature, and timely corrective actions. Cross-reference rainfall data with inspection dates. Conduct quarterly internal audits of monitoring records.
  - *When*: Ongoing review of logs; formal compliance evaluation quarterly and after any discharge event.

---

### **Obligation 5: OSHA Excavation & Trenching Safety**
- **Requirement**: Comply with 29 CFR 1926 Subpart P for any excavation > 5 feet deep. Implement protective systems (sloping, shoring, or shielding), designate a Competent Person to conduct daily inspections, and ensure all workers have trench safety training. Provide cave-in protection and egress means every 25 feet.
- **Source**: 29 CFR 1926.650-.652; OSHA Directive CPL 02-00-161
- **Applicability**: Applies to all grading, utility trenching, and foundation excavation activities. As a homebuilder with 60 employees, the company must designate and train a Competent Person for each site.
- **ISO Clause**: ISO 45001:2018 6.1.3 (hazard identification); ISO 14001:2015 6.1.3 (indirect – soil disturbance environmental aspects)
- **Evaluation (9.1.2)**:
  - *How*: Daily documented inspections by Competent Person. Monthly safety audits by corporate safety manager. Review incident reports and near-miss logs. Verify training records during annual OSHA compliance audit.
  - *When*: Daily during active excavation; formal evaluation monthly and after any trenching incident.

---

### **Obligation 6: Sediment Basin & Buffer Requirements**
- **Requirement**: Install a temporary (or permanent) sediment basin for the 25-acre common plan of development since total disturbance exceeds 5 acres. Maintain 25-foot undisturbed buffer zones around perennial waters (if present) or 50-foot buffers for trout streams. Stabilize basin outlets and remove sediment when capacity is reduced by 50%.
- **Source**: Georgia Rule 391-3-7-.07(6)(a); GA-G870000 Part II.C
- **Applicability**: The 3.5-acre phase is part of a 25-acre development, triggering basin requirements even if this phase alone is < 5 acres. Must be addressed in the overall SWPPP.
- **ISO Clause**: ISO 14001:2015 6.1.3 (pollution prevention); ISO 45001:2018 6.1.3 (indirect – flooding hazards)
- **Evaluation (9.1.2)**:
  - *How*: Pre-construction inspection to verify basin design and location. Monthly measurement of sediment accumulation and structural integrity. Include in weekly stormwater inspection checklist.
  - *When*: Before upstream disturbance begins; monthly during active construction; after major storm events.

---

### **Obligation 7: Local Cobb County/Marietta Ordinances**
- **Requirement**: Obtain Cobb County building permit and comply with Cobb County Development Standards (Sec. 34-81) for erosion control. If within Marietta city limits, comply with City of Marietta Land Development Code (Sec. 11-8) which may require additional silt fence specifications and tree protection measures.
- **Source**: Cobb County Code of Ordinances Ch. 34; City of Marietta Land Development Code; Local NPDES MS4 Permit
- **Applicability**: All construction within Cobb County jurisdiction. The company must determine if site is in unincorporated Cobb County or Marietta city limits.
- **ISO Clause**: ISO 14001:2015 6.1.3; ISO 45001:2018 6.1.3
- **Evaluation (9.1.2)**:
  - *How*: Verify permit conditions during pre-construction meeting. Conduct quarterly inspections for ordinance-specific requirements (e.g., tree save zones, silt fence type). Review any code enforcement notices.
  - *When*: Before permit issuance; quarterly during construction; within 24 hours of any code violation complaint.

---

### **Obligation 8: Recordkeeping & Annual Reporting**
- **Requirement**: Maintain all permits, SWPPP, inspection logs, corrective action documentation, training records, and NOT for at least 3 years post-project. Submit annual NPDES compliance evaluation report to Georgia EPD by January 30th each year. Report any non-compliance incidents within 24 hours to EPD and local authority.
- **Source**: GA-G870000 Part V; O.C.G.A. §12-7-19; 40 CFR 122.41(j)
- **Applicability**: Required for all permit holders. The 60-employee company must designate a records custodian.
- **ISO Clause**: ISO 14001:2015 6.1.3 & 7.5 (documented info); ISO 45001:2018 6.1.3 & 7.5
- **Evaluation (9.1.2)**:
  - *How*: Quarterly internal audit of record completeness and retention. Annual third-party review of reporting accuracy. Use checklist to verify all required elements are documented.
  - *When*: Quarterly for internal audits; annually by January 30 for NPDES report; within 24 hours of any reportable incident.

---

### **Obligation 9: Final Stabilization & Permit Termination**
- **Requirement**: Achieve final stabilization (70% vegetative cover or equivalent) on all disturbed areas before terminating permits. Submit NOT to Georgia EPD and close LDA permit with local authority. Remove temporary controls only after stabilization is verified.
- **Source**: GA-G870000 Part II.E & III.D; Georgia Rule 391-3-7-.07(9)
- **Applicability**: Required for all phases. The 3.5-acre phase must be stabilized before NOT submission.
- **ISO Clause**: ISO 14001:2015 6.1.3; ISO 45001:2018 6.1.3 (post-construction hazard removal)
- **Evaluation (9.1.2)**:
  - *How*: Conduct final site inspection with photo documentation of stabilization. Submit NOT and obtain written approval. Verify no active discharge points remain.
  - *When*: Upon phase completion; final compliance audit within 30 days of NOT approval.

---

### **Obligation 10: Contractor & Subcontractor Oversight**
- **Requirement**: Ensure all contractors/subcontractors (e.g., grading, utilities, landscaping) comply with SWPPP and ES&PCP. Include erosion control requirements in contracts, provide pre-mobilization training, and audit contractor performance weekly. Company remains legally responsible for violations by subcontractors.
- **Source**: GA-G870000 Part II.B; O.C.G.A. §12-7-6 (liability); OSHA Multi-Employer Citation Policy
- **Applicability**: As the general contractor/developer, the company has "control" over the site and is the "operator" under NPDES. Applies to all contracted work on the 3.5-acre phase.
- **ISO Clause**: ISO 14001:2015 6.1.3 & 8.1 (operational control); ISO 45001:2018 6.1.3 & 8.1.4.2 (contractor management)
- **Evaluation (9.1.2)**:
  - *How*: Prequalify contractors for environmental/safety competence. Conduct weekly joint inspections with contractor reps. Review contractor training records monthly. Include compliance in contractor payment holdback provisions.
  - *When*: Before contractor mobilization; weekly during active work; at contractor demobilization.
